parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no facility ban, no documented police targeting or sweeps. Structural positives: legal gender recognition since 2013 with an operating framework for police/customs/prison searches of trans persons, hate-crime law covering gender identity, a prosecutor enforcing accommodation rights, Pride events with official participation, and travel guidance describing broad acceptance. No universal-exposure or organised-targeting tier features appear. Negatives: documented enforcement gaps (inadequate hate-crime investigation, uneven judicial handling, under-reporting), escalating anti-gender political rhetoric including a parliamentary 'Gender Ideology' session, and one Pride disruption — societal-hostility-tier friction with imperfect but existing recourse. Border/entry treatment and custody placement are open questions, which per the rubric weigh far lighter than exposures. This fits the 0.75 profile: real protection, imperfect enforcement, social friction, no traveler-facing restriction.
